reason: The cited lines show browser_snapshot returns the current browser page URL, title, and ARIA/page snapshot via socket messages. That establishes reading browser/page content, which can include non-public data reachable in the user's browser/session, so SECRET is supported. The returned page snapshot/title/URL are page-controlled content, so UNTRUSTED is supported. The lines do not show arbitrary host code execution, only socket messages to browser functions, so HOSTEXEC is not supported. They also do not show sending agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination; the data is returned to the caller, so SINK is not supported.
